parsed.attack: A weeknight household cooks a rotation of fifteen to twenty-five recipes, so the binder is exhausted in about five weeks and the scanning - the act the product is actually about - goes to zero by construction rather than by boredom. What remains is a list-combiner over a closed set, and the list defeats it: a household cooking its standing rotation buys nearly the same things every week, so after a month the shopping list is memorised and the app is competing with something the shopper can write from memory in ninety seconds. Their own kill line concedes the shape of it, at fewer than 20% reaching ten pages in sixty days.
parsed.strongest_defence: The Saturday shop is one of the most reliably recurring triggers in domestic life and it never stops, and the corpus is genuinely theirs - handwritten family cards that exist in no database anywhere - so once digitised the binder gets used repeatedly even after it stops growing. It is also a one-time purchase, so a tool used hard for five weeks and lightly thereafter has already been paid for; there is no renewal to fail.
parsed.verdict_reason: The weekly shop and the one-time price genuinely blunt the surface, but the corpus closes within about five weeks and the resulting list is near-identical each week, so memory competes with the product.
